answer: Histories are stored in ripple, checked in opal, and jetty shows each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 6 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. A farm cannot present clean aliases since the record follows the key, so laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 1932 identities would post 1696 proofs and burn roughly 51 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
